utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Haynes. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls who are present. I don't see the witness. Are there any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, briefly. First of all, just a bit of the housekeeping and schedule. We, the Prosecution, is not going to be calling Witness 183. We have decided not to call that witness. That's Danilo Zoljic. He's not a protected witness. And he was scheduled for later on in this week. What we intend to do is to call an investigator to talk about the Muslim identification book and explain what that book is and what it shows. What we would propose to do is have our investigator Erin Gallagher testify about that book. She is not on our witness list so we would be seeking to add her just for that topic. It's something which Mr. Blaszczyk could do. He's been our sort of catch-all for everything that comes up as an investigator. He's on the list. But we would like to give him a bit of a break at the moment and he's got other things I'm sure he needs to work. And I don't think there is any prejudice in that because it's really something that any investigator could do once they look at the exhibit and learn about it. I know in other cases that I've been on we have listed initially on our witness list an investigator will discuss how this picture was obtained or something like that. So that is our plan and what we hope to do following Witness 164 who is available today, Mr. Petrovic, Pirocanac. And one further point, I've discussed this with Mr. Ostojic, the way we plan to proceed if it's all right with Your Honours is we'll finish this entire testimony concerning the Muslim book, cross-examination -- road book, excuse me, cross-examination and any redirect. Then Mr. Ostojic will finish his cross-examination regarding the Drina Corps collection. I think I'll have a short redirect and then we can move to the next witness. That's our plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you confirm that, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, before we proceed any further, what are your comments, if any, about the Prosecution request to add a new witness, Erin Gallagher to testify on the Muslim ID book? The alternative is, obviously, that it will be dealt with by Mr. Blaszczyk himself, so I see no point in -- this anyway, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, my learned friends from the Prosecution. Concerning this change, we've exchanged a few e-mails and letters with our friends from the Prosecution on that topic. What Defence teams request, at least the Nikolic Defence, was that they forward a short 65 ter summary for this witness so that we would know what his testimony would be in regard of the book. Since she did not participate in the collection of statements, based on which the people from the book were identified, we haven't received a summary, therefore we are still waiting for that and the material provided by our learned friends so that we would know about the subject matter of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Yes, Mr. Nicholls? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We could certainly do a short 65 ter summary. I don't think it's absolutely necessary because if I give you a little bit of information on the book, this is virtually the same with some corrections. It's the same Muslim identification book which has been exhibited in the two prior trials. It contains pictures of persons from the videos and their names and explains how they've been identified either by themselves for some people who made it through these events or whether they've been identified by family members or others. So what the investigator will do is explain really what's in the book and how it's put together. There is not going to be a whole lot of information coming in from outside the book but I can provide something very short, I think, which explains how that is going to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that would be better. I think that would be better. So for the time being, I take it that there are no radical or fundamental objections to this witness being brought over to deal with this piece of evidence rather than Mr. Blaszczyk himself. Am I right in thinking so? I know that silence is golden but ... All right. Thank you. So I would take it that this would be the procedure we will be following. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are also thinking on this subject matter based on our respective past experiences whether there is indeed any need for a witness to come and testify on this book. Obviously, if there is going to be a cross-examination, then obviously the need for a witness arises. But there is agreement between the two sides that the book will be tendered and the information you seek to produce arises or shows on the face of the book itself, then perhaps you can agree to dispense with the need of a witness. But if there is even one single Defence counsel that wishes to cross-examine anyone in particular on this Muslim ID book, then obviously you need a witness. But in any case, message is if you require a witness, the witness is going to be allowed to testify. If you come to an agreement that you can dispense of a witness, please let us know and we can proceed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, and I'll talk to my friends, Your Honours and see if we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Anything else? Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'd like, if we can, to go into private session and raise this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to finish off the chapter that we were discussing yesterday and then we'll revert to your previous testimony with Mr. Ostojic's cross-examination. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could just continue, we were in chapter 4, Zeleni Jadar, at pages 70 and 71. When we left off, we were nearing the end of this presentation, at least in pages. I think about 20 minutes or slightly less of video and we will just continue and stop at a couple of places. If we could play it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is not in the book but I've stopped it at 48.26. We've just seen the car moving now again, shooting out of the window of the car and we were passing a couple of large buildings. Can you tell us where Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin are going, which direction they are heading in now and where they are?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are going towards Srebrenica. This is an overview of Srebrenica from the hills above Srebrenica on the way from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And, Your Honours, if we could go now to pages 66 and 67 of the book, 2986. The reason for that is there is one chapter which just have a few pictures of Srebrenica and it has the pictures that we saw yesterday on the way to the wood factory and also on the way back rather than splitting the town photos up into two sections. Yes, 66 and 67. I think we have 76 on the monitor. That's right. Thank you. And if we could continue to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now at just about the frame on page 66 A. Can you tell us where this is, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Srebrenica. The car is moving towards the centre of Srebrenica, to the place close to this market mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could continue to the next photo on page 66 B?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now at approximately the photo on page 66 B. And you've marked it here but this is -- well, you tell us where we are, please?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are in the centre of Srebrenica. This is the street between the market in Srebrenica, market square, and the department store in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Actually, Your Honours, it's not a question for Mr. Blaszczyk but we've included these photos so that later it may help to identify places on a different video. If we could continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. We are now at page 74 B which is the last chapter 5, Mosque Azemina. This is, I think, quite self explanatory but where are we now, Mr. Blaszczyk, in the video and which direction is Mr. Petrovic heading in?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are at the edge of Srebrenica. This is Vidikovac settlement and the car with Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic is driving towards Bratunac, Potocari, Bratunac, and we see the picture of the mosque located in this Vidikovac settlement. And on page 75, I attached two current pictures of the same mosque. The first picture, picture number 1 from page 75, this is the same -- the view from the side of Srebrenica, from the direction of Srebrenica, of the same mosque. And on the picture number 2 from page 75, this is view of the same mosque but from direction of -- from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. We can play now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is just before the end at 1.00.28.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know where this is, just this last big hills we see just before the tape ends?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last hill is according to Witness Petrovic, it was recorded in Serbia already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can stop. Thank you. I don't have any other questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Does any one of the Defence team wish to cross-examine the witness? Let's go through the list first. I had the Popovic team asking for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, we have no questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. The Beara team wanted 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will a have a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, please. Unless there is an agreement with some other Defence team that they go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I have a couple --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have a couple questions just to follow up on some of the points that my learned friend asked you. When he asked you yesterday about the software that was used to put together this book, I think on page 60 and 61 you stated that it was used -- or Zoran Lesic is the person who actually used the software and created this?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the person Zoran Lesic. He created, yeah, he created this presentation with my help of course. I was present during this presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever find the name of that software?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew the name and I believe this is VR Worx, and plus Photoshop, of course. And it was played in QuickTime player.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, what part of this presentation or this -- that you shared with us today, what part was created by Zoran and which was created by you? I know you mentioned that you participated in it but --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean technically it was created by Zoran Lesic, but I was present during this creation. I confirmed all the locations and I was the person who pointed out where we should put the particular places or pictures, how we should play with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can have 65 ter 1517 up on the screen, please? While that's coming up, sir, you mentioned this and it's an aerial photograph that you mentioned on page 32, line 17, on yesterday's transcript. I just have a couple of questions on that, if you don't mind. Well, I think I can still ask the question until they get up on the screen because I'm sure you're familiar with it; it's the aerial photograph on the 13th of July in Potocari. Can you tell me more about that aerial photograph? From whom did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is aerial photograph from our exhibit list. I don't remember right now from where we received it, but I believe it was aerial photograph from US.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I know it's on the exhibit list. I'm asking for the source. As you sit here today under oath, do you know if it was aerial photograph that the United States government provided to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is -- this is the photograph provided to us by the government of US.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who put the markings on this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who put the top caption that's in the box which states overview of Potocari, Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who added the red numbers on the right-hand side of that box that's on the top centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's evidence unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Evidence unit --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is evidence unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where in the United --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, evidence unit, it's our ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'm only stopping because I think we are overlapping a little bit and I apologise to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not a little bit, a lot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We are overlapping a lot. Just so I'm clear, sir, in this centre box that's presented here on the right-hand side, that's the evidence unit's identification number that they placed on this document here in The Hague after they received it from the US government, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This red letters with number were put by evidence unit. This is our ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what about the date that appears immediately below the box that's in the centre of the page, 13 July 1995? Who placed that there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. When did you receive this aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was long time ago, before I arrived when I joined the Tribunal, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did you assist also in selecting that this photograph be used as part of the presentation that you're going to give in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who made that selection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, being the lead investigator at least for the last year and a half plus, and being the -- playing that role in the years that you have as second in command, can you tell me what efforts you undertook to determine not only the source of the documents but who may have placed the writing in yellow on this photograph? Did you do any inquiries into that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know anyone who did, who was under your command or superior to you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about with respect to the box that's in the centre of the page that we see where it's identified as overview which has the red ERN number on it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And would it be the same answer for the date that falls underneath that box in the centre page?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was created by investigators before me who used to work for this case much before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And are you speaking of a particular investigator, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a group of investigators, more than right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that under the leadership and tutelage of Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we are done with that exhibit. Sir, I want to just clarify, if I may, the point because in the beginning of your testimony yesterday, you mentioned that you received several copies of this Petrovic video: One from the BBC, one from himself, one from the Ministry of Defence and I think also one from Studio B, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware about any copy from Studio B. I know that we received a copy from broadcast of Studio B from Mr. Borovcanin and another copy we received from Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So there is only two copies that you received, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are speaking about the copy of Studio B broadcast, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in all fairness, I know that it was the Studio B broadcast that came as you've identified it from Mr. Borovcanin. So is it just those two videos that you had in your possession and you showed us the difference between the two where you felt it was edited, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are referring to the Studio B edited programme, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now, you mentioned though in your testimony that you also received a copy of the Petrovic video from BBC in 2002. What was that about then?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know but I know that we received a copy from BBC of the raw material -- the copy of the raw material from Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about the copy of the Petrovic video as you identified it from the Ministry of Defence in 2007?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, is that also a copy of a video that you received that is similar or the same as that -- those copies of videos that you received from either Studio B or from Mr. Borovcanin or Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also the copied material of the raw material of Mr. Petrovic as the BBC copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the 2007 video from the Ministry of Defence was the same material which you identify as raw material that you received from Mr. Petrovic identified as the BBC copy, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I have on this issue and I think with the Court's permission we will come back to the Drina Corps collection a little later today. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Madam Nikolic, no cross-examination. Mr. Stojanovic, you had asked for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go through a couple of exhibits in order to eliminate any misunderstandings that may have arisen from yesterday's evidence. Let us look at P02478 first, please. And while we are waiting for this exhibit to appear, I will only let you know that this is one of the aerial photographs of the industrial zone in Potocari. Which is ERN number 01068728, 01068728. And can Madam Usher assist us in providing Mr. Blaszczyk with a pencil in order for him to make certain markings? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, I believe that we can orientate ourselves as to the buildings or facilities that are involved here. I suppose it wouldn't be much of a difficulty for you to identify the buildings?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please use the pen that you have and mark with a cross the place where you located a group containing Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin and Mr. Kingori on the 13th of July in front of the white house, as you called it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please mark the place where the entrance into the UN base in Potocari was?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't have everything an X. So if you put an arrow -- you know, you can cancel that mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher will assist you. You can erase it and then do it again and just put an arrow sort of mark.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should mark as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just an arrow indicating the entrance or following the entrance to the compound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please place the letter O or a circle on the place where the observation post used by the UN base was, if you know where it was located, of course?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean OP? Or observation post in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether it fits in this photo but, the nearest OP, I doubt it having been there, I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Blaszczyk, we are not talking about the OP Papa, that's the closest. Rather, I'm referring to whether you know whether there was an observation post within the UN base compound in Potocari, in fact the site that you were just looking at.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the left side of the road heading towards Srebrenica. But I am not 100 per cent sure, but I am thinking that the place is close to -- close to entrance to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate with a circle roughly where the observation post was?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of your familiarity with the place, can you give us the approximate distance between the place you marked with a cross as the place where Mr. Borovcanin, Kingori and the others were and the place you marked with an arrow as the entrance leading into the UN base. In your estimate, what is the distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about 50 metres, the distance is about 50 metres from the entrance to the UN base to the place where Mr. Kingori and Borovcanin were standing in the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You'll agree with me that there were no obstacles there impeding the line of sight toward the building that we refer to as the white house?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please place today's date at the bottom there and your signature because we will not be needing this. It's the 4th of December and your signature, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday in your testimony inter alia, at page 18626, lines 6 to 8, you said the following: Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin stopped their vehicle between the white building and the blue building, the distance between which was some 100 to 150 metres. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember but I think I said that I think that they parked the car over there because the first footage we have, we started from in the front of -- from the -- of the front from white house and Feros building. They started to recording the events in the front of the Feros building and white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please look at an aerial shot of the Dutch base which is P0153 -- 523? While we are waiting for the shot, I just wanted to tell you, Mr. Blaszczyk, that this is one of the aerial shots dated the 13th of July, around 2.00 p.m. According to what you know, does that tally to -- with the time at which such photographs -- those photographs were approximately taken? For the transcript I wanted to repeat that this is P01523. While we are waiting for the photograph, Mr. Blaszczyk, my question was: Since it says in the transcript that some time of taking the photographs was mentioned, the 13th of July, around 2.00 p.m., does that correspond to the time when Mr. Pirocanac's footage was made and you referred to it yesterday regarding Potocari?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we see the footage of Mr. Petrovic, we can see, I think, that the first time code is about 1500 hours, taken on the 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct if I say that when looking at the photograph before us, that that part of the road between the white house and the blue factory, such as you indicated, was full of vehicles, buses, trucks, civilians, and UN vehicles?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The car in which Borovcanin and Pirocanac came, would it be logical that it be left in front of the Dutch base and that they continue on foot from the blue factory to the white building -- from the white house to the blue factory, especially keeping in mind everything that was recorded on that day in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that at this moment, you cannot tell us precisely where the car had been stopped and what part the cameraman went on foot to cover the distance between the white house and the blue factory?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. I cannot tell the precisely the place where they parked the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at another photograph from the set before you. It is P02986. Page 12, photographs B and D. You'll see it on the screen and you also have it in front of you. It is your set, page 12, photographs B and D. I suppose you have the photographs in front of you. Am I correct in saying that in that entire area in Potocari, there were back-packs, bags, items, clothing left, and maybe the most of it was where the armed personnel carriers of the Dutch Battalion were as can be seen from the photograph D. By analysing the footage and the photographs, would one be able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see some rubbish, some box over there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at a short excerpt from the footage that we also saw yesterday. It is V 0006747. Prosecution Exhibit P02054. The time is 6.56 to 7.02. I believe that should be approximately the time reference. We'll wait for the excerpt to be shown. While waiting, I just wanted to say that that excerpt is where we can see the blue factory, the truck, the tractor and Mr. Borovcanin, Kingori, and my questions will have to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that on this still we can see a red tractor towing a white water tank with the letters UN?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the discussion among those present is taking place in front of the tractor and the tank with the UN letters?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have some additional questions regarding this topic for some other witnesses. On the same footage, and the same exhibit, could we please go to 13.40 to 13.50? That part of the footage is something we saw yesterday, Mr. Blaszczyk, as well. The APCs and some music in the background. I wanted to remind you yesterday at page 18633, pages 11 through to 15, said that you believe that the music that can be heard was actually playing in the vehicle where Zoran Petrovic was. Let us all have another look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe the time is right. It is indeed 13.40 to 13.50 on the footage. What do you base your conclusion on, mentioned yesterday when you said that you believed that the music that can be heard was played in the vehicle where Zoran Petrovic was?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Zoran Petrovic together with other person that followed this armed vehicles and they parked these armed vehicles before, and he started to recording -- to record these armed vehicles when they were shooting and he was standing next to his car when he -- which he used to follow these vehicles. And the only explanation for me that it could be hear music from this car because it's -- this is some distance from these armed vehicles and the shooting would be quite dangerous to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you today exclude the possibility that the music in the background was actually edited on to the footage before it was released for TV broadcast?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I cannot exclude such situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we still have the armoured vehicles in front of us, I wanted to ask you about what you could conclude based on the footage referred to. Would these armoured vehicles be Pragas with anti-aircraft or anti-tank cannons, guns?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it seems that they are Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the reason for which, on the interactive CD we saw yesterday, you termed this armoured vehicles Praga or was that because of something else?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first vehicle is a Praga. The second one is also the armed vehicle used by the forces, and the Praga is the first one. Sorry, could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Based on what you've just told us, on the interactive CD we saw yesterday during your testimony, at the bottom, well, it says that it is a Praga, that the armoured vehicle is a Praga.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I put any marks in this interactive presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not go back to it unless necessary but it is 502987, and it says, "Praga" on that photograph. Do you remember that or do you think that I'm stating this incorrectly?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The exhibit is P02987.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to see this footage first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you for your assistance, then, so that we can see that part together. The CD is P02987. Those photographs are titled, "Praga 1" and "Praga 2." Could you please find that so that we have a look at it together?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You're right. I marked this place as Praga 1 and Praga jedan [phoen] but I referred to the location rather than the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that this was Pervani village and that on the interactive CD, you marked the two photographs as Praga 1 and Praga 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this since it may be of importance when discussing who could have had such vehicles in their possession. Is it within your knowledge and please tell us if it is not, whether this indeed is a Praga or maybe it is a Pat or an anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the first vehicle seen on the picture now, I don't know, this is a Pat vehicle and the second one is a Praga.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, when you say that one vehicle is a Pat, do you mean the one further away from us or closer to us?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to us, the one closer to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the more distant vehicle, you believe is a Praga, is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us have a look at P01562. While waiting for it, Mr. Blaszczyk, I wanted to tell you that it is one of the shots of the Kravica warehouse, an aerial shot, taken on the 13th of July, as marked on the photograph, the date is the 13th of July 1995, around 2.00 p.m. Can you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The bus closer to the building and closer to the western entrance of it, and that is something you referred to yesterday, can you confirm to me that it is in the exact spot as you explained yesterday based on the footage excerpt taken by Zoran Petrovic, Pirocanac? And please bear in mind also what you had on the topic during the interactive presentation.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is not correct. No, this bus is not located in exactly the same place which was shown by me yesterday during the presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say - and I'm not setting a trap or anything, I'm just trying to get an answer from you - is it fair to say that the bus on the shot of Zoran Petrovic was closer to the western entrance as described to you or, rather, closer to the right-hand side of the photograph and of the warehouse, therefore?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was closer to the western side of the white -- of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us approximately how many metres that is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 30 metres, 30 metres, 30, 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 30 to 40 metres. To the west, compared to the current position of the bus?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, about even less but for sure few metres, more than 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also agree that on the footage referred to yesterday, and analysed by you, made by Zoran Petrovic, there is no evidence or trace of two buses being there at the time when the footage was taken or there was only one bus there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this footage it's visible only one bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Comparing this photograph with Zoran Petrovic's footage, can we conclude that within an interval, both buses moved, the result of which was that one was gone and the other bus or some other bus which arrived in the meantime was moved some 20 metres to the west?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is possible, is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Having in mind that you said yesterday that you were at the location at least 50 times, perhaps you can use this photograph to tell me something, if not we can use another one. In any case, will you agree with me that between the entrance to the warehouse and the western gate, the distance between the two can be covered in the following way: From the road, from the direction of Konjevic Polje, one can turn to the right on a side road, cover the distance of some 30 to 40 metres and then turn right again to enter the warehouse compound?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no objection but I'm just not -- what is exactly referred to by entrance to the warehouse? It's not -- it may be just me but it's not completely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps it would be more practical to look at another Prosecution Exhibit. Perhaps we can put it on the ELMO. I believe it would be much clearer from it. We can also provide another copy to the Prosecutor so that they can verify that indeed it is their exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it in e-court or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is in e-court. However, I only have the ERN number at this moment. I don't have the exhibit number. That is why I asked for it to be done this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you tell us the ERN number, I think we can easily trace it, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 02683858 [sic], I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't see anything as yet. I can see the picture but I can't see the number. 02683858, he said, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You're right, you have to turn to the right, you have to pass about 30 metres, turn right again, and you can reach the eastern part of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time for a break in order to reorganise our cross-examination. We will provide exhibit number for this photograph after the break and I will have a few questions left and then conclude with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. And also consider this during the break, because on page 24, line 23, you had referred -- and this is what prompted Mr. Nicholls to intervene -- you had referred to the possible distance between the entrance to the warehouse and the western gate. And now the witness is speaking of an eastern part of the warehouse. So I think we need better bearings because that -- the way you have described it and he has answered, I find it confusing. If necessary, please, Mr. Blaszczyk, be prepared to mark the photo if we have located it on e-court. You mark it for us so that we can understand better. Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Blaszczyk, shall we start with the point I raised before the break? We will mark exactly what you intended when you put the question to the witness and what he meant when he answered you so that we can see clear what distance he's talking about, or you both are talking about. Mr. Blaszczyk, I'll read out to you -- you said, you are right, you have to turn to the right, pass 30 metres and turn right again and you can reach the eastern part of the warehouse. And we are talking as starting from the entrance, I take it, Mr. Stojanovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In order to be practical, we agreed that we would now take the pen and indicate the route toward the -- that particular side of the warehouse, to make it clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, I believe that the way I put the question we understood each other correctly. If we go, take the road in the direction of Konjevic Polje and we turn toward the Kravica warehouse where the vehicles we referred to were, can you please indicate the direction of movement with arrows?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that would be the movement from the direction of Bratunac toward the entrance into the Kravica warehouse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. From direction of Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that now -- or let me ask you now to take the blue pen, to mark the route you would take from the direction of Konjevic Polje toward the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the same route, we have to get the same road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, okay, now, at the beginning of the first arrow you drew, could you write, "K" for Konjevic and "P" for Polje, please? No, the blue arrow, that is coming from which direction, from Konjevic Polje or from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The blue arrow is coming from direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I asked to you write, Konjevic Polje, here. Okay. And next to the other arrow, which is coming from Bratunac direction, could you put a B, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for your assistance. For the record let us state that this is the P1563 exhibit that we are using and can I ask Mr. Blaszczyk to place today's date, the 4th of December, at the bottom of the page together with your signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And we can put this photograph away now. Thank you very much. Thank you. Let us look at another exhibit now, Prosecution Exhibit P02103, page 107 of the book used during the presentation by Witness Jean-Rene Ruez. There, we will also see a photograph of the Kravica warehouse. Mr. Blaszczyk, this is my question while we are waiting for the picture. In view of the fact that you stated yesterday that you were present in front of the Kravica warehouse on several occasions, to the best of your recollection and based on what you were able to conclude by analysing the footage of Mr. Pirocanac and by analysing this photograph which was taken back in 1996, could you conclude that the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road and the yard of the Kravica warehouse were separated from each other by a wire fence running in front of the warehouse in relation to the road?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. We can see the wire fence in front of the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this fence stand there today?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, if today, I believe so, yes, I believe. It looks not the same but I think it's a little bit higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have no further questions on this subject. In several footage clips we analysed yesterday, you saw and you indicated yourself that the date and the time appeared in the corners of the screen when referring to the footage by Mr. Petrovic/Pirocanac. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge, could you state whether the time indicated on the footage corresponded to the time at which in fact the footage was made or were there possible discrepancies in terms of shorter intervals of time, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm and I cannot deny it. According to Mr. Petrovic, he had no experience to operate with this video camera, he couldn't know how to put the proper time on the video camera. But I believe this is the proper time because -- at least the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back once more to the aerial photograph of Potocari which is P1517? That's the photograph we used at the start of cross-examination today. Can you take the pen again and place a circle on the DutchBat base, as you will see it on the picture? Before we look at this photograph, can we go back to P2478? That was the picture we used first, 2478, P2478. That's the picture we used at the start of examination today, in fact. That's the photograph, Mr. Blaszczyk, we had at the start, where you indicated the position of the white house and the blue factory. I'd like you to mark the entire compound of the DutchBat base on that photograph. That's precisely the photograph. Thank you. Can I kindly ask you to mark the UN base compound?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what I want to ask you in relation to the photograph: The facility or the building in front of the building you called the white house, what is it? Or what was it in July of 1995? What was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is the former Feros company building, the factory and building in front of the road leading from Bratunac to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it at any point in time in July of 1995 used for the purposes of the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you were able to see while analysing the yesterday's footage, were you aware of the fact that there were members of the DutchBat there and the refugees from Srebrenica, the population that fled Srebrenica on the 12th and the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analysing my picture from the road book, it's difficult to say that they were the members of UN DutchBat inside and refugees from Srebrenica. On the pictures we see only the group of the people walking on the right and on the left side of the road towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you do not rule out the possibility that the population that fled Srebrenica was indeed present in that part of the industrial zone of Potocari in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude that -- such possibility but I don't remember on the statement of the witness who was located in this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know at all that the group of fleeing people were accommodated in that part of the Potocari industrial zone that was held by the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the group of the people were also accommodated in DutchBat base in Potocari, and because there were no more place for the people, from the refugee from Srebrenica, they were also located in bus compound, Zinc company and Energoinvest company buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Can you place today's date and your signature on this photograph? And that would conclude my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Fauveau, do you have a cross-examination? You had asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci. The Gvero Defence team have no cross-examination. Mr. Sarapa, do you have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [In English] No, we don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think there is a re-examination, Mr. Nicholls, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Extremely brief, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, you were asked by Mr. Stojanovic about the conclusion you made, you spoke about of the music coming from the car during the portion of the video where we see fire directed into the hills. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether you asked during the interview of Zoran Petrovic in 2006, do you remember if you asked him about that music?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sure we asked him about this music but I don't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what his answer was?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Would it help you remember if I showed you the statement?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe this is highly improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, it's not. I'm refreshing his recollection. The interview -- I'll let my friend finish. Well, if he's finished, it's simply this, Your Honour: The basis of his conclusion was put into question. This was a topic that was gone over with the witness in the interview, in April -- February and April 2006 and the question was asked, he remembers asking the question. I think I'm just trying to refresh his recollection and I think it's completely a normal procedure to refresh on this topic. It was over a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I may very briefly reply. This is the next witness. We can ask him this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The issue is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, the issue is not to get in this vital piece of information of where the music is coming from. It's because there was a challenge to his -- to Mr. Blaszczyk's basis for saying where the music was coming from and saying, well, you haven't been able to tell us how you concluded that. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We believe that this issue could probably be dealt with much better by Mr. Petrovic instead of the witness. However, since the witness has given us his opinion and he's also been asked on cross-examination on how he formed this opinion, we think you have a right to pursue the matter. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm referring to page 127 of the interview, lines 24 to 27, Mr. Blaszczyk, I'll just read it out since it's not in e-court. In this portion of the video you asked the question of Mr. Petrovic, is that music coming from your car? And he answered: From the car because the car is there, yeah, I was next to the car. Does that help you remember how you came to your conclusion about the music?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You read me back the transcript from this interview. I asked this question and I got answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. That concludes your testimony on this chapter. However, as you may have heard earlier on, I think you were already present in the courtroom, maybe, maybe not, we are going to proceed now with Mr. Ostojic's continuation of his cross-examination on the subject matter that you testified upon a couple of weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I understand you are going to be called again later on to testify again; is that correct, Mr. Nicholls? Or -- according to the information that we have, you're going to summon him again to testify on the duty officer's notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is all subject, Your Honours, to our discussions with the Defence and, hopefully, possibly working out some kind of agreement or stipulation on these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. So let's see how it works out, Mr. Blaszczyk, and you may need to come back. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, we're now going to focus our discussion back to the Drina Corps collection that you seized, I think, in 2004, if you don't mind. Sir, in our last discussion before an objection was raised by my learned friend, I was simply inquiring of you as to who was personally supervising the transfer of the Drina Corps collection to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was given by Colonel General Andric at that time but according to the witness Nebojsa Vukicevic, it was supervised -- the transport was from Zvornik to Mali Zvornik, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me this: Who -- and you found this information when, sir, recently or did you find the information since you seized the documents in 2004?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the information about --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As to who is personally supervising the transfer of the Drina Corps collection to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information by OTP, we received a statement of Nebojsa Vukicevic in, I believe, in between May and October 2004, before the collection was seized in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you also, sir, remember getting a letter from Republika Srpska addressed to the ICTY in March of 2005 also identifying that the transfer of the documents were under the direct command of Lieutenant-Colonel Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that it was such letter but I would like to see this letter to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. I'll be happy to give it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a letter that was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor dated the 3rd of March 2005, and I have a hard copy for the witness signed by Mr. Jovan Spajic. With the Court's permission if the usher can hand that to -- if I may, Your Honours, just to speed it up, direct his attention to page 2 and I put a little asterisk or an arrow in the significant portion for this question, but he's welcome to look at the document in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So let me ask you this, sir: Also not only personally supervising the transfer of the Drina Corps documents, is it true that in fact Dragan Obrenovic was the person who had the keys to the padlocks that contained those documents in Mali Zvornik, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan Obrenovic had a key from this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you being the lead investigator did you come to learn that anyone else had a key during that time period of approximately one year that those documents were at Mali Zvornik other than Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, I should refer to the statement and testimony of protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And why don't we go quickly with the Court's permission into private session so that I can just make sure we are talking about the same witness, Your Honour, to get the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, being the lead investigator on this team and involved Srebrenica did you obtain from any other individual or source that other than this individual that you said testified in private session, did anyone rebut or contradict Mr. Vukicevic's statement that Dragan Obrenovic is the only person who had the keys to the two padlocks to the storage?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you learn from any witnesses that you interviewed whether or not any other individual maintained any such sets of keys?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you -- do you know, sir, as I'm sure you do, and isn't it correct that it was Dragan Obrenovic who was responsible for the storage of the Drina Corps collection while it was at Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, again we should refer to those two statements, statement of Nebojsa Vukicevic and protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again I'll ask you then as the lead investigator in the Srebrenica case, did you obtain information from any other witnesses or documents which would contradict what Mr. Vukicevic said?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, if I may, sir, please?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to Mali Zvornik location?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I am. Up until March of 1999, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the evidence that in March of 1999, the warehouse or the storage area where the Drina Corps collection was held was broken into?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is also mentioned in the Nebojsa Vukicevic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, share with me this: As the lead investigator in the Srebrenica case, what did you do to either confirm or to determine who broke into the storage facility which contained these documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing, me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about anyone on your staff?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about anyone who preceded you in your position or in your staff before you arrived at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down a little bit, Mr. Ostojic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And he told you that he hasn't got any information about it which means neither before nor during nor after.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if an index was made of the Drina Corps collection before the documents were moved to Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the location of the Drina Corps collection was after they were removed from Mali Zvornik in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The collection ended up in Gornji Milanovac. We have only this information. Whether it was transferred from Mali Zvornik to Milanovac directly or were kept in any other places, we don't know. We cannot exclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know for what period of time that you would have a gap in this chain of custody, if you will, for the Drina Corps collection before you identified that they were kept at Mali -- in Milanovac?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have no information, in fact, where the collection was kept between March, at least March 1999 and December 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now it's my understanding, sir, that Dragan Obrenovic tendered to the Prosecution documents on two separate occasions in 2003, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were any of the documents that he provided to the Office of the Prosecution part of the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember right now but I think that most of these documents were part of the Drina Corps collection, according to the description of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this question, sir: With respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Nicholls and Mr. McCloskey, if my memory is not failing me, let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic, please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just so we have a clear record, Mr. Obrenovic tendered documents to the Prosecution both in June of 2003 and September 2003, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that the documents that he provided to the OTP were in part that from the Drina Corps collection as we've come to identify them, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this question, sir. If could you tell me who is responsible to analyse the Drina Corps collection for purposes of compliance with Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in team.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that include yourself, obviously, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Include myself as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your understanding is of Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my understanding is to find all information or the facts, mitigating facts and all information we can say that the accused can be innocent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about with exculpatory facts, sir, or do you just look at mitigating facts?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also all the facts we can say that Prosecution evidence are not reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you create an index with the information that you provide to the Prosecutor specifically that you undertook in connection with analysing the Drina Corps collection to be in compliance with Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you communicate that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We inform our lawyers from our team.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's what I assume but do you do it orally or do you do it in writing, by memo form, e-mail?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly by e-mail or just giving the copy of the documents to them personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Blaszczyk, please slow down a little bit. Short pause between question and answer so that the interpreters' life doesn't become more difficult than it already is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that this same type of analysis and responsibility that you undertook with the Drina Corps collection you and everyone at the OTP would undertake that obligation for all other collections and documents, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you still maintain records of your analysis with respect to the Drina Corps collection and that which may be exculpatory or, as you say, mitigating pursuant to Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did do you a search recently to determine if you maintained those documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, did you undertake this specific analysis with respect to the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, why not, if you're the lead investigator in the Srebrenica case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was busy with another task.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, earlier you testified that everyone was involved in this responsibility and analysis of Rule 68 in connection with the Drina Corps collection. Can you identify for me which investigators under your command, sir, were responsible to do that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody is obligate to identify all documents in regards to Rule 68, and each investigators which can see such document should inform our lawyers about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, and I heard that now for the second time and thank you for that, but everybody includes you and yet you didn't do it, correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember [indiscernible] document which I identified as Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask about, if I may, your obligations as a professional investigator and a member of the Office of the Prosecution. Do you agree with me that you have a professional duty when a witness misstates something and you have evidence that he's wrong on his recollection, that you should correct him on his recollection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should analyse this information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you also agree with me that it's not only a professional obligation but it's also an ethical obligation?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And not only professional and ethical but it's a legal obligation, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, to analyse the possible Rule 68, yeah, this is legal obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you're switching -- my question wasn't limited just to Rule 68, sir, I'm asking you specifically given than you've informed us that you've interviewed witnesses (redacted), is it your professional, ethical and legal obligation, if the witness makes a statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I could just restate the question, Your Honour, because I'm not sure if the witness, with all due respect, fully understood. Sir I'm moving away from Rule 68 and the obligations that we discussed previously. I'm asking you do you have a professional, ethical and legal obligation when you interview a witness and if you know that the witness has misspoken or did not recall properly, to inform the witness that in fact he's incorrect by showing him documentation or other testimony to refresh his recollection on that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to this particular witness we spoken about, I think he was -- he was confronted with the statement which stated totally different things when he stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm, sir, talking generically here for the moment. I'm saying with any witness. Isn't it true that you have a professional, ethical and legal obligation if a witness, for example, says, that I was in Potocari on this date but you have evidence that he was, for example, in Pale on that given date and at that given time, is it not your professional, ethical and legal obligation to share with him that documentation so that he could refresh his recollection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my way. I would say to the witness that I have another information but I'm not going to disclose the -- it's not my habit to disclose that to the witness the source of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is that also the policy of the investigators who work under you, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends of the -- of the way how they conducting the interview or they conducting the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- but, as you know, the -- we investigators are coming from different countries and they have different experience and different way to do their investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'm more interested in how you do your investigation, sir, in particular if you failed to at least tell the witness that you have information that would either refresh his recollection or contradict that which he's sharing with you, what would that constitute in your mind, if not a breach of your professional, ethical and legal duties?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assure you that I have clear conscience.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm not testing your conscience here; I'm asking you if there was a breach of that policy that you enunciated here to us that you wouldn't show him the document but that, in fact, you would share with him the information would that be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, stop. Please proceed to your next question. We've had enough of this. I think he's already excluded the possibility that you're putting to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll put this down as a marker, Judge. We had a clear deal with Mr. Meek that the cross-examination would not exceed 30 minutes. That was the agreement why we agreed to defer this, and I'm not making a huge fuss about it but now we are well over 30 minutes. This exactly what we wanted to avoid was a long, burbling fishing expedition cross being deferred until Mr. Ostojic got back. That's why we agreed to the half hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In my estimate, you haven't been 30 minutes as yet but --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- anyways, I'm going to check and you continue in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll try not to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try not to burble or garble anything for the Prosecution but I'd like to ask this witness concretely.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, ever interview Mr. Ljubisa Beara, my client's driver?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you interview him or just meet him?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I met him. I prepare the information report but because at that time, as far I remember, there was no time and even was very difficult to interview him because I met him at his house, in -- at his home in Han Pijesak. And he was called for interview again to Sarajevo, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And based on your recollection, sir, do you remember that you did not at any time share with Mr. -- or Mr. Beara's driver any documents like a vehicle log?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our meeting in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember showing him any documents at that stage, but I informed him that we call him for the official interview in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you remember, sir, in Sarajevo, if you showed him any documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I am pretty sure that interview in Sarajevo was conducted by my colleague but I cannot refer right now to the transcript of this interview but I'm pretty sure that I wasn't present during this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, other than failing to show that driver vehicle logs from the Main Staff, do you have a recollection whether or not you showed him any statements for other witnesses which would help us get to the truth as to where Milos Tomovic and Mr. Beara were on certain given points? Do you remember sharing with him any information from other witnesses, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
